title: Qubit-environment entanglement in pure dephasing dynamics for mixed initial states
authors: Małgorzata Strzałka, Nico Peters, Laura Ares, Jan Sperling, Katarzyna Roszak
abstract: Decoherence of qubits is one main limitation in quantum information processing, where the qubits themselves can be mixed because of decoherence and additional decoherence may generated through interactions with a bath. Here, we present a complete study of qubit-environment entanglement in the case of interactions that lead to pure dephasing of the qubit by allowing the initial state of the qubit to be mixed, exceeding previous restrictions. We find that the criteria for separability that hold for pure initial states of the qubit are reduced to witness status. Yet, the evolution of the witnesses reflects the array of features that entanglement can exhibit in the mixed case but are forbidden in the pure-qubit case. Most notably, this includes sudden birth of entanglement as the initial phase of the evolution is typically separable. Moreover, there is a stark numerical advantage to the study of entanglement for large environments when using the witness rather than the traditional measures available. We include the study of entanglement generated between a spin qubit and a sparse spin environment to illustrate the peculiarities of the evolution of entanglement in this case, as well as to emphasize the level of reliability of the entanglement witness.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical study of qubit-environment entanglement during pure dephasing, crucially extending the analysis to mixed initial qubit states. It demonstrates that for mixed states, entanglement diagnostics rely on entanglement witnesses, revealing complex dynamics like the sudden appearance of entanglement. The findings highlight the limitations of simple separability criteria and emphasize the utility of advanced diagnostic tools like minimal eigenvalues.
main_problem: The study investigates qubit-environment entanglement (QEE) dynamics under pure dephasing, specifically extending the analysis to cases where the initial qubit state is mixed, overcoming previous theoretical restrictions.
main_result: For mixed initial states, the criteria for separability reduce to an entanglement witness, and the entanglement dynamics can exhibit features like the sudden birth of entanglement, which are forbidden for pure initial states.
method: The authors use entanglement witnesses, including minors and minimal eigenvalues derived from the partially transposed density matrix, to diagnose separability and entanglement in the joint qubit-environment state.
model_or_system: The model involves a single qubit interacting with an environment (bath) via an interaction causing pure dephasing. The system is analyzed using the joint density matrix evolving under the influence of the environment.
key_observables: Qubit-environment entanglement (QEE), separability criteria, entanglement witnesses (minors and minimal eigenvalues), and the evolution of these quantities over time.
important_parameters: The initial coherence of the qubit ($\epsilon \in [0, 1]$) is a critical parameter distinguishing pure ($\epsilon=1$) from mixed ($\epsilon<1$) initial states.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an initially uncorrelated state ($\hat{\sigma}(0) = \hat{ho}(0) \otimes \hat{R}(0)$) and focuses on pure dephasing interactions.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the evolution of normalized entanglement witnesses for different numbers of environmental spins, showing discrepancies between the minors and the actual entanglement behavior (birth/death) for mixed initial states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general framework for pure dephasing (Section II), then analyzing QEE for pure initial states (Section III), and finally focusing on the extended and more complex case of QEE for mixed initial states (Section IV).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems as it provides advanced diagnostic tools (beyond simple criteria) to quantify entanglement in realistic, decohering solid-state qubits (like NV centers) whose initial states are often mixed.
